chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding the mature woman who proposes marriage to herself, he said: 'She has more right over herself; she may entrust her affair to whomever she wishes, provided he is her equal (kufu'), after she has previously been married to a man.'

key_terms.أَمْلَكُ بِنُ بِنَفْسِهَا: She has more right/authority over herself
key_terms.اَلثَّيِّب: Mature woman (one who has been married before)

ai.seo_question: Does a mature woman need a guardian to marry in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that a *thayyib* (mature woman who has been previously married) retains full agency over her marriage contract, distinguishing her status from a *bikr* (virgin) who typically requires guardian consent. The condition of *kufu'* (compatibility) ensures that her choice aligns with social and religious standards, reflecting the Imams' emphasis on female autonomy in marital affairs while maintaining communal harmony.
